title: Causal Latency Attributor for per-request inference KPIs
creator: Priya Menon
description: Goal: build an attribution layer that decomposes end-to-end inference latency into causal components (ingress routing, network, request queuing, scheduler/kernel scheduling, model runtime compute, KV cache hit/miss, model-variant fallback). Output stable derived metrics and trace-enriched tags that power per-route/model latency SLOs, root-cause dashboards, and automated regression alerts. This ticket covers design + a prototype sidecar collector and the metric/trace enrichment rules required for a safe canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype sidecar collects OTLP spans and Prometheus scrape metrics and emits a per-request 'latency.attribution.*' metric series (per-stage breakdown) with stable labels (tenant, route, model, variant, cache_hit)
Backfill join between trace_id and per-request counter to produce aggregated per-route P50/P95/P99 by attribution bucket for dashboards
No more than 1% additional p99 latency observed on canary nodes under synthetic traffic during initial rollout
Automated tests validate attribution correctness using synthetic trace fixtures (including cache-hit/miss and fallback scenarios)
Runbook documented with steps to disable/roll back and instrumentation links for debugging
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight sidecar (go) deployed with runtime frontdoor that consumes OTLP/Jaeger spans and Prometheus metrics; correlates spans to per-request metric envelopes via deterministic request-id header; emits derived OTLP metrics (or Prometheus pushgateway) with attribution labels

Trace hooks: add shallow span annotations at known runtime boundaries: ingress-router, request-queue, batch-assembly, kernel-scheduler, model-exec, kv-cache-check, response-serialize. Each span includes 'stage.start'/'stage.end' timestamps to compute durations deterministically
Sampling: support deterministic 1% forced-sample across tenants for full span capture; sidecar should gracefully degrade to aggregated metrics when spans missing

Metric naming: latency.attribution.total_ms, latency.attribution.net_ms, latency.attribution.kernel_ms, latency.attribution.kv_ms, latency.attribution.queue_ms. Use snake_case to align with Prometheus conventions and add 'tenant' and 'route' labels

Aggregation: sidecar emits low-cardinality rollup metrics for dashboards and high-cardinality per-request envelopes to internal event store for debugging. Provide retention policy for per-request envelopes (30d for enterprise)

Schema: derived metric envelope is simple key/value label map; avoid nested JSON; follow existing OTLP proto fields. Backward-compatibility: provide 'legacy.labels' mapping for dashboards depending on older keys
Backpressure: sidecar must apply bounded queueing and drop non-critical high-cardinality envelopes when CPU > 70% or ingestion backlog grows; emit 'latency.attributor.dropped_envelopes' metric
Security: strip PII from tags; do not emit full request payloads. KMS/role permissions enforced by runtime environment
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: design brief posted to docs (link below); initial schema draft reviewed with Observability team
2026-03-09: integration test harness added to synthetic-inference-runner; validated attribution on synthetic cache-hit/miss flows
2026-03-11: design review with runtime and console owners; agreed on metric names and rollback criteria; queued for canary in 2026-W12
notes: Trade-offs: full-span instrumentation everywhere increases cardinality and ingestion cost. We mitigate by emitting compact derived metrics and small-sample per-request envelopes for debugging.
Rollout plan: canary on 2 pods in staging -> synthetic load test -> one production region limited tenant rollouts -> gradual scale with telemetry monitors
Monitoring: create alerts on 'latency.attributor.dropped_envelopes > 100/min' and attribution divergence between trace-derived and existing coarse latency metric > 10%
